title: Secure entitlements experiment: pricing, contract language, and authorization commitments
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Run a controlled experiment to determine the optimal way to surface SSO/SAML and RBAC as contract-level entitlements vs. priced add-ons. We need packaging that balances sales velocity, deal size, and legal / security review overhead while preserving predictable unit economics for Redwood Inference. This ticket coordinates experiment design, contract wording changes, sales enablement, telemetry, and questionnaire updates.

Scope:
- Define three packaging variants to test (bundle vs add-on vs role-gated tiers).
- Draft contract clause templates and addenda (terms for SSO attestations, RBAC guarantees, data isolation commitments).
- Implement feature-flagged entitlement gates in Console for pilot customers.
- Instrument conversion and legal-review metrics in our CRM and Console.
- Create playbook and FAQ for Sales/SEs.

Success metrics / hypotheses:
H1: Bundling SSO+RBAC into enterprise plans increases ARR per closed deal by >=12% without reducing win rate by >5%.
H2: Offering SSO as an add-on lowers time-to-sign for mid-market accounts but increases legal review activity for enterprise (>30% more Qs).
H3: A role-tier gating model (basic RBAC in core plan, advanced RBAC in enterprise) reduces support load while keeping perceived value high.

Key stakeholders: Product (Maya), Legal (Priya Singh), Sales Ops (Ethan Chen), Solutions Eng (Sofia Martinez), Engineering (Liam O'), Security & Compliance (Andre Gomez).

Artifacts and links:
- Draft clause templates: drive.google.com/drive/folders/secure-entitlements-drafts (see v2 clauses)
- PRD: drive.google.com/documents/enterprise-entitlement-prd-v1
- Feature flag work (engineering): github.com/redwood-inference/console/pulls/4522
- Sales enablement doc: drive.google.com/documents/entitlements-playbook-v1

Risks / trade-offs:
- Bundling increases baseline ARPU but may reduce deal flexibility for customers that require only limited controls.
- Add-on pricing complicates billing and may create support friction for partial entitlement adoption.
- Strong contract commitments (e.g., guaranteed RBAC role definitions, escalations) increase legal exposure and require SLOs from the runtime team.

Required decisions:
- Which packaging variant to run against which segments (e.g., new logos vs renewals vs mid-market)?
- Minimal contract language acceptable to legal without deep customization for each deal.
- Instrumentation and dashboard requirements to measure legal review load and sales friction.

Next steps (see comments for owners & dates):
1) Legal to produce final clause set for each variant (Priya) — due 2025-02-25.
2) Engineering to add entitlement feature flag + telemetry events (Liam) — initial build by 2025-03-07.
3) Sales Ops to select 30 pilot opportunities and enable A/B allocation (Ethan) — list by 2025-02-28.
4) SEs to prepare onboarding checklist and templates (Sofia) — ready by 2025-03-03.

This ticket should be used as the single source of truth for the experiment. All customer questionnaire responses during the pilot should be linked back here for pattern analysis.
